title: CVISS Member Agencies - LexisNexis/Accurint Data Sharing Agreements (Sacramento Police Department)

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: CVISS Member Agencies - LexisNexis/Accurint Data Sharing Agreements (Sacramento Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

1) All MOUs, contracts, addendums, or other legal documents signed by your agency and LexisNexis (and subsidiaries, including LexisNexis Risk Solutions, Accurint, AVCC, PSDEX, etc.). This may include (but is not limited to) a LexisNexis Consortium Sub-Agency Addendum, Schedule A, or other agreements.
2) Any MOUs or other agreements between your agency and CVISS or Sacramento County Sheriff related to sharing RMS/CAD data.
3) Agency Configuration Page: A printout of your agency's AVCC configuration page. Please include the full page, including any other agencies listed on the same page. Example Screenshot: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1G_J35fnmu7qZO_k8UOoVHFcd_R2HKXVg/view?usp=sharing

Context: We understand that CVISS moved to the LexisNexis Accurint platform to share data among CVISS member agencies. We are seeking to understand whether your agency and other CVISS members share contributed data with agencies beyond the consortium (e.g., the Public Safety Data Exchange / PSDEX national database), or whether data sharing is restricted to CVISS members only. Often LexisNexis Sub-Agency Addendums allow agencies to choose whether they share nationally or only within the consortium - we seek to understand what your agency chose to do.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Shawn Segal

communications.subject: RE: California Public Records Act Request #26-1955
communications.communication:
Hi Anna,

I am looking for documents from 1/1/2022 through present - with a few caveats that will hopefully make the search easier:
A) I only need one copy of each document type. If you've signed a few contracts with LexisNexis over the years, I only need the most recent. 
B) For request #1, the most important document I am looking for is titled "AVCC XML Addendum." It's typically attached to a Schedule A and Master Service Agreement (MSA) which I'd love as well, but the AVCC XML Addendum is what dictates whether your data is shared nationally or only with consortium members - and that's the question we're trying to answer. 
C) For #2, if this yields dozens of results, we only need a few of the most recent examples - not every single one. Some consortiums sign new ones each year and I don't need the entire history - just the most recent several. 
D) Same with #3 - we're only looking for most recent info. If you cannot find the screenshot, this alternative export will also work:  An export of what data you share with CCM and other law enforcement agencies. This is often called a Data Classification Crime Results sheet. To obtain this, an account admin can click a link on the left-hand side under admin permissions called 'Data Classification Manager.' There is an Export link on the top right of the Data Classification Manager page. Depending on the LexisNexis product(s) you subscribe to, this may have a different name or location. We are looking for the list of data you share with LexisNexis, and who your share it with (CCM only, or also other law enforcement agencies?) [Only an CCM/Accurint Account Administrators can access these documents]

Thank you,
Shawn

title: LexisNexis Accurint Virtual Crime Center (AVCC) PSDEX Data Sharing Agreement (Austin Police Department)

communications.subject: Texas Public Information Act Request: LexisNexis Accurint Virtual Crime Center (AVCC) PSDEX Data Sharing Agreement (Austin Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Texas Public Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

This request is focused on Accurint Virtual Crime Center (AVCC) and Public Safety Data Exchange (PSDEX), both are products of LexisNexis Risk Solutions (LNRS / RELX). We are making this request because we found evidence that your agency likely uses, has access to, or contributes data to AVCC (directly or indirectly). If your agency has no relationship with these products, please tell us so.

We are seeking records that indicate whether your agency contributes data to AVCC/PSDEX, and if so, what other agencies have access to that data. 
--
We are requesting the following records:
1) All signed contracts, addendums, amendments, or agreements between your agency and LexisNexis that are currently in effect or were in effect at any point between 1/1/2020 and the date this request is fulfilled.  
[CONTEXT] Common documents include "AVCC XML Addendum" / "Schedule A" / "Master Terms & Conditions" / "sub-agency agreements" / "joinder agreements" or other similar agreements. If your agency contributes data or gets AVCC access through a consortium or fusion center, please include the MOU or similar agreement outlining that AVCC relationship. 
2) AVCC Usage Logs. 
 - 2.A) If your agency shares data with AVCC/PSDEX, please provide query logs of who has accessed your agency's data and what reason/case number they provided while searching your agency's records. We understand some of these reports are generated by LexisNexis rather than stored locally; please include any such report your agency has received or can obtain. Please provide in CSV or XLSX format where available. If you are unable to see logs of how your agency's data is used by other agencies within AVCC, please indicate so. 
3) AVCC Configuration:
 - 3.A) Agency Configuration Page: A printout of your agency's AVCC configuration page. Please include the full page, including any other agencies listed on the same page. Example Screenshot: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1G_J35fnmu7qZO_k8UOoVHFcd_R2HKXVg/view?usp=sharing 
 - 3.B) Configuration Explainer Documents: Typically documents with details on what data LexisNexis recommends that you contribute, and what they recommend you exclude. Sometimes this may be called "FAQs and FYIs for Exclusions", or may include integration suggestions for an interface with your RMS/JMS/CAD systems. 
--
PRIORITY: The two most important documents we seek are your signed AVCC XML Addendum and 3.A. - The AVCC agency configuration page printout. 
SEARCH TERMS: To aid in your search, we recommend the following search terms: "AVCC" "Accurint" "PSDEX" "Public Safety Data Exchange" "Public Safety Marketplace" and "Accurint Virtual Crime Center"

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

communications.communication:

Austin Police Department - R188896-061126 
Re: Open Record Request of June 11, 2026, Reference # R188896-061126 
Dear Shawn Segal, 
The Austin Police Department received a Public Information request from you on June 11, 2026, to request copies of records pertaining to the following: “To Whom It May Concern: 

Pursuant to the Texas Public Information Act, I hereby request the following records: 

This request is focused on Accurint Virtual Crime Center (AVCC) and Public Safety Data Exchange (PSDEX), both are products of LexisNexis Risk Solutions (LNRS / RELX). We are making this request because we found evidence that your agency likely uses, has access to, or contributes data to AVCC (directly or indirectly). If your agency has no relationship with these products, please tell us so. 

We are seeking records that indicate whether your agency contributes data to AVCC/PSDEX, and if so, what other agencies have access to that data. 
-- 
We are requesting the following records: 
1) All signed contracts, addendums, amendments, or agreements between your agency and LexisNexis that are currently in effect or were in effect at any point between 1/1/2020 and the date this request is fulfilled. 
[CONTEXT] Common documents include "AVCC XML Addendum" / "Schedule A" / "Master Terms & Conditions" / "sub-agency agreements" / "joinder agreements" or other similar agreements. If your agency contributes data or gets AVCC access through a consortium or fusion center, please include the MOU or similar agreement outlining that AVCC relationship. 
2) AVCC Usage Logs. 
- 2.A) If your agency shares data with AVCC/PSDEX, please provide query logs of who has accessed your agency's data and what reason/case number they provided while searching your agency's records. We understand some of these reports are generated by LexisNexis rather than stored locally; please include any such report your agency has received or can obtain. Please provide in CSV or XLSX format where available. If you are unable to see logs of how your agency's data is used by other agencies within AVCC, please indicate so. 
3) AVCC Configuration: 
- 3.A) Agency Configuration Page: A printout of your agency's AVCC configuration page. Please include the full page, including any other agencies listed on the same page. Example Screenshot: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1G_J35fnmu7qZO_k8UOoVHFcd_R2HKXVg/view?usp=sharing 
- 3.B) Configuration Explainer Documents: Typically documents with details on what data LexisNexis recommends that you contribute, and what they recommend you exclude. Sometimes this may be called "FAQs and FYIs for Exclusions", or may include integration suggestions for an interface with your RMS/JMS/CAD systems. 
-- 
PRIORITY: The two most important documents we seek are your signed AVCC XML Addendum and 3.A. - The AVCC agency configuration page printout. 
SEARCH TERMS: To aid in your search, we recommend the following search terms: "AVCC" "Accurint" "PSDEX" "Public Safety Data Exchange" "Public Safety Marketplace" and "Accurint Virtual Crime Center" 

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes. 

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not. 

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires. 

Sincerely, 

Shawn Segal

I will keep you updated and will provide as soon as possible. 
Thank you for contacting the City of Austin. 

PIR Team 
APD Open Records

Records maintained by a contractor in connection with a governmental function

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Flock Safety ALPR Records (Contracts, Audit Logs, SB 34, Communications) (Petaluma Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I request the following records concerning any products, services, platforms, sensors, or data feeds of the following categories, whether currently used, previously used, piloted, trialed, or formally considered by this agency, for the period January 1, 2020 through July 6, 2026:

Automated license plate reader ("ALPR") and connected-camera systems — including but not limited to Flock Safety (Flock Group Inc.), Motorola Solutions / Vigilant Solutions (LEARN, PlateSearch), Genetec (AutoVu), Axon / Fusus, Rekor, Leonardo/ELSAG, Neology, and Digital Recognition Network (DRN);
Data-integration, analytics, and "real-time crime center" (RTCC) / "real-time awareness center" (RTAC) platforms — including but not limited to Peregrine Technologies (peregrine.io), Palantir, Fusus (Axon), SoundThinking, and any comparable platform that aggregates, links, or searches across agency data sources; and
Any product beyond ALPR cameras offered by the above vendors (e.g., Flock's Condor PTZ video, FlockOS, Nova, or other data-intelligence products; Peregrine's data-integration or AI/"safety flagging" modules).

Where a term below refers to a Flock-specific feature (e.g., "Organization Audit"), please read it to also request the equivalent record in any other vendor's system.
1. Contracts and procurement. All contracts, master services agreements, order forms, amendments, renewals, statements of work, quotes, proposals, purchase orders, invoices, and payment records with any vendor identified above, including any data-processing addenda / data-processing agreements (DPAs), memoranda of understanding (MOUs), and any competitive-bid waivers or sole-source justifications.
2. Vendor communications. All communications (email, text/SMS, letters, meeting notes, calendar invitations) between agency personnel and representatives of any vendor identified above (including the vendor's @flocksafety.com, @peregrine.io, or equivalent domains), concerning procurement, deployment, configuration, camera or sensor siting, pilot / early-access / free-trial programs, and any product beyond ALPR cameras.
3. Search and audit logs. The complete audit/usage logs showing each search or query, including — for Flock — the "Organization Audit" and "Network Audit" logs (Flock Insights dashboard), and — for any RTCC / data-integration platform (e.g., Peregrine) — the user access and query logs. For each entry, please include all available metadata fields, e.g.: record ID, user name, organization/agency name, date/time of search, license plate or query terms, stated reason, case number, camera count, time frame searched, filters, search type, and any text/AI prompt. Please export in the system's native machine-readable format (CSV/XLSX), not as a PDF printout, and do not strip metadata fields.
4. Hotlist and NCIC configuration (commonly the most important item). Records sufficient to show the full hotlist configuration of any ALPR system, including a screenshot, screen capture, printout, or CSV of the hotlists the agency subscribes to. This specifically includes which FBI NCIC "topics" are enabled and, in particular, whether the "Immigration Violator" file / topic is enabled, and the date any such topic was enabled or disabled. Also include any custom hotlists created by the agency.
5. Data sharing and external / federal access. A list of all external entities with which data is shared or from which it is received, and the settings governing that sharing, including:

The agency's Flock network-sharing settings, and whether "National Lookup" and/or statewide lookup are enabled, with the dates access was granted, modified, or revoked;
All external agencies that can access this agency's data, and all agencies whose data this agency can access, with dates;
Specifically, any access by or sharing with federal agencies — ICE, CBP, HSI, ATF, FBI, DHS — including records of searches those agencies (or other agencies on their behalf) ran against this agency's data;
All MOUs, data-sharing agreements, and network-participation terms (e.g., with a fusion center such as NCRIC), and any restrictions placed on downstream use or re-dissemination.

6. California ALPR statutory records (SB 34 and amendments).

The record of access required by Civil Code § 1798.90.52;
The agency's current ALPR usage and privacy policy required by Civil Code § 1798.90.51 (and, if the agency is an ALPR end-user, its policy under § 1798.90.53);
The results of the annual audit of ALPR searches for compliance with the usage/privacy policy (Civil Code § 1798.90.53), including any assessment of whether non-hotlist data was purged within 30 days of collection;
Any records concerning use of ALPR for immigration-enforcement geolocation or retention beyond 30 days (see Civ. Code § 1798.90.5 et seq., as amended).

7. Camera / sensor deployment and locations. Records sufficient to show the number, type, and locations of all cameras or sensors installed in the jurisdiction (fixed ALPR, mobile ALPR, PTZ/video, gunshot-detection, or other), their installation dates, and any encroachment, right-of-way, or other permits issued for their installation.
8. Data sources integrated into any data-integration / RTCC platform. For any platform identified above (e.g., Peregrine), a list of all data sources, feeds, and databases integrated into or accessible through the platform — for example computer-aided dispatch (CAD), records management systems (RMS), body-worn and in-car camera footage, fixed/traffic/school cameras, ALPR data, jail/booking data, DMV or state databases, and any third-party or commercial data sources — together with any system-configuration or data-source inventory documents.
9. Retention, governance, and training. Records reflecting data-retention periods and deletion practices, access controls (who is authorized to search and what approvals are required), prohibited uses, training materials, and internal policies, standard operating procedures, directives, or general orders governing use of any system identified above.
10. Misuse, breaches, and oversight. Any audits, reports, internal-affairs records, complaints, disciplinary records, or communications concerning suspected or confirmed misuse of any system (including searches for personal, immigration, or reproductive-health-related reasons), and any records of data breaches or security incidents involving the data.
11. Surveillance-use policy and impact reports. Any Surveillance Use Policy, Surveillance Impact Report, Privacy Impact Assessment / Data Protection Impact Assessment, or comparable document required by any applicable local surveillance-oversight ordinance, relating to ALPR, RTCC, or data-integration technology generally or to a specific vendor.
12. Governing-body review. Staff reports, resolutions, meeting agendas, minutes, and presentations to the city council / board of supervisors / oversight body concerning approval, funding, or renewal of any contract identified above.
13. Confirmation of non-use. If the agency has never used, piloted, or contracted for any ALPR, connected-camera, RTCC, or data-integration system of the kind described above, please confirm that in writing.

Format, preservation, and processing

Machine-readable format. Please provide records in their original electronic, machine-readable format with metadata intact (Gov. Code § 7922.570); spreadsheets and logs as CSV/XLSX, not PDF printouts.
Preservation. Because some responsive records (particularly ALPR search/audit logs) may be subject to short retention or automatic deletion, I request that the agency preserve all responsive records — and suspend any automatic purge of responsive audit logs — pending completion of this request.
Segregability and exemption log. If any record is withheld in whole or in part, please identify each record and the specific exemption claimed (Gov. Code § 7922.540), and release all reasonably segregable portions (Gov. Code § 7922.525). Data describing how the system operates and is used — as distinct from information about a specific individual — is generally not exempt investigative material (see ACLU of S. Cal. v. Superior Court (2017) 3 Cal.5th 1032). Personal information may be redacted while still disclosing system-level records.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robbie Powelson

Superior Court (1999) 74 Cal.App.4th 1008, the court upheld the withholding of personal contact information of complainants on the ground that disclosure could deter citizens from interacting with local government and frustrate legitimate enforcement efforts. title: Law Enforcement Equitable Sharing Request Information

communications.subject: Nevada Public Records Act Request: Law Enforcement Equitable Sharing Request Information
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Nevada Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

• A copy of all TDF-92 "Request for Transfer of Property Seized/Forfeited by a Treasury Forfeiture Fund Participating Agency" submissions for the period Jan. 1, 2023 through Sept. 21, 2026. A blank version of the form can be found at https://home.treasury.gov/system/files/246/Seized-2011-Property-Form-TD-F-92-22-46-OMB-1505-0152.pdf
• A copy of all Equitable Sharing Request Forms (DAG-71) submitted by this agency to the U.S. Department of Justice for the period Jan. 1, 2023 through Sept. 21, 2026. A blank version of the form can be found at https://www.justice.gov/file/485791/dl.
• A copy of all annual Equitable Sharing Agreement and Certification submissions for the period Jan. 1, 2023 through Sept 21, 2026. A blank version of the form can be found at https://www.justice.gov/criminal/media/1446466/dl?inline
• Any spreadsheet, index, or other umbrella document maintained by this agency that reflects equitable sharing requests made by this agency for the period Jan. 1, 2023 through Sept 21, 2026. Please include all available segregable information, including the nature of each request, the monetary value of each asset, and the final disposition of the request (i.e. was the request successful or not). 

This request is being made by a journalistic researcher. It is being made for research purposes, not commercial ones. Please assess fees in accordance with provisions for media requesters. In the event that this agency decides to charge this requester fees not to exceed the actual cost of reproducing the records, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request.

Please fulfill this request electronically, preferably by e-mail attachment, if available.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response within the statutorily-mandated timeframe. 

Sincerely, 

Patrick File

Dear Requester, 
Attached are your requested records pertaining to request, records pertaining to 2023-9410. 
Certain information has been redacted from the records under Exemption 6 (personal privacy information). In determining to withhold such information, FDA considered 5 USC 552(a)(8)(i), when applicable, and whether FDA reasonably foresees that disclosure of such information would harm an interest protected by the relevant exemption(s) and whether disclosure is prohibited by law. 
This now closes your request with the agency. 
In accordance with 45 CFR § 5.61 and 21 CFR § 20.41(b)(5), you have the right to appeal this determination. Your appeal should clearly identify the agency determination that is being appealed. It would be helpful if you provide specific reasons explaining why you believe the agency's adverse determination should be reconsidered. By filing an appeal, you preserve your rights under FOIA and give the agency a chance to review and reconsider your request and the agency’s decision. Your appeal must be mailed within 90 days from the date of this response, to: Director, Office of Management and Enterprise Services, U.S. Food & Drug Administration, 5630 Fishers Lane, Room 1050, Rockville, MD 20857, or emailed within 90 days from the date of this response to FDAFOIA@fda.hhs.gov. Please clearly mark both the envelope and your letter “FDA Freedom of Information Act Appeal.” Items arriving or delivered after 5 p.m. Eastern Time will be deemed received on the next workday. (mailto:FDAFOIA@fda.hhs.gov) 
If you would like to discuss our response before filing an appeal to attempt to resolve your dispute without going through the appeals process, please contact FOI-OC-Group@fda.hhs.gov. (mailto:FOI-OC-Group@fda.hhs.gov)

If you are unable to resolve your FOIA dispute through our FOIA Public Liaison, the Office of Government Information Services (OGIS), the Federal FOIA Ombudsman’s office, offers mediation services to help resolve disputes between FOIA requesters and Federal agencies.

communications.subject: Georgia Open Records Act Request: Flock Audit Logs Dunwoody October - December 2024
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Georgia Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Copies of all audit logs, search logs, or usage reports related to your agency's use of Flock "ALPR" systems for the period October 1, 2024 through December 31, 2024. This includes but is not limited to the "Organization Audit" and "Network Audit" logs available in the Flock software's "Insights" section, showing records of license plate searches performed by agency personnel, timestamps of searches, user identification information (names, badge numbers, or user IDs), and any associated case numbers or investigation references.

Please provide records in their original electronic format (CSV, Excel, or similar).

To the extent any portion of these records is claimed exempt under the Open Records Act, I request that the exemption be applied at the field or column level rather than by withholding entire logs, consistent with the segregability requirement of O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(b)(1)(A). If a specific field (such as the free-text search justification field) is withheld, please identify which field and the specific statutory basis for withholding it.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jason Hunyar

communications.subject: DC Freedom of Information Act Request: Interagency Briefings & Damage Reports: Morris Rd SE Stormwater Landslide
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the DC Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

TO: ddot.foia@dc.gov, doee.foia@dc.gov, foia.synergy@dc.gov

CC: hsema.foia@dc.gov, oig_hotline@epa.gov, earl.eutsler@dc.gov, rwhite@dccouncil.gov, swilson@dccouncil.gov, callen@dccouncil.gov, ldonovan@wusa9.com, tkopania@wusa9.com
Subject: EXPEDITED FOIA DEMAND: Hazard Assessments & FEMA Region 3 Communications (1488-1500 Morris Rd SE)

To the FOIA Officers and Executive Leadership of D.C. HSEMA and DOEE:

Under the District of Columbia Freedom of Information Act (D.C. Official Code § 2-532), I am formally demanding the immediate release of the following public records pertaining to the active 25-foot landslide, federal MS4 infrastructure failure, and compromised public canopy located within the 1488 to 1500 block of Morris Rd SE.

This request specifically encompasses, but is not limited to, the following mandatory disclosures:

1. FEMA Communications:
All correspondence, emails, memorandums, and official requests sent from D.C. HSEMA, DOEE, or the Mayor's Office to FEMA Region 3 regarding the life-safety hazard and structural collapse at this specific location.

2. Hazard Mitigation Assessments:

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Department of Defense support for TV series "Did They Fix That?"
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Any documents pertaining to collaboration between the Department of Defense (DoD) and the production of the TV series "Did They Fix That?" (2023-). Such documents may include but should not be limited to: script notes; production assistance agreements; and all records of communications between employees of DoD and members of the cast, crew, and production company of "Did They Fix That?," including memos, notes of meetings and conference calls, emails, and other forms of communication.

"Did They Fix That?" appears on a list of DoD entertainment industry collaborations released to me through FOIA. The list is attached to this request.

I am the Director of Research Operations at a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization called The Decoding Culture Foundation as well as the editor-in-chief and a contributor to a research magazine published by said foundation titled "Cultural Engineering Studies." These documents will be used for public education and research purposes. I therefore request a waiver of all fees that may otherwise apply. Attached is a document with organization letterhead confirming my position, as well as the organization's 501(c)(3) application and approval form.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Brett Carollo

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Request: Zbigniew Brzezinski
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

This is a request under the Freedom of Information Act.  I hereby request the following records:

Records relating to or mentioning Zbigniew Kazimierz Brzezinski AKA Zbigniew Kazimierz Brzeziński, March 28, 1928 – May 26, 2017. He was a Polish-American diplomat and political scientist. He served as a counselor to President Lyndon B. Johnson from 1966 to 1968 and was President Jimmy Carter's National Security Advisor from 1977 to 1981. Brzezinski belonged to the realist school of international relations, standing in the geopolitical tradition of Halford Mackinder and Nicholas J. Spykman. See the attached obituary for proof of death.

Please conduct a search of the Central Records System, including but not limited to the Electronic Surveillance (ELSUR) Indices, the Microphone Surveillance (MISUR) Indices, the Physical Surveillance (FISUR) Indices, and the Technical Surveillance (TESUR) Indices, for both main-file records and cross-reference records for all relevant names, agencies, organizations, companies and events including but not limited to those cited in the previous paragraphs and/or attachments. If previously released records are available, then I request a rolling release consisting of those records while additional records are located and processed for release.

I am a member of the news media and request classification as such. I have previously written about the government and its activities for AND Magazine, MuckRock and Glomar Disclosure and have an open arrangement with each. My articles have been widely read, with some reaching over 100,000 readers. As such, as I have a reasonable expectation of publication and my editorial and writing skills are well established. In addition, I discuss and comment on the files online and make them available through the non-profit Internet Archive, disseminating them to a large audience. While my research is not limited to this, a great deal of it, including this, focuses on the activities and attitudes of the government itself. As such, it is not necessary for me to demonstrate the relevance of this particular subject in advance. Additionally, case law states that “proof of the ability to disseminate the released information to a broad cross-section of the public is not required.” Judicial Watch, Inc. v. Dep’t of Justice, 365 F.3d 1108, 1126 (D.C. Cir. 2004); see Carney v. U.S. Dep’t of Justice, 19 F.3d 807, 814-15 (2d Cir. 1994). Further, courts have held that "qualified because it also had “firm” plans to “publish a number of . . . ‘document sets’” concerning United States foreign and national security policy." Under this criteria, as well, I qualify as a member of the news media. Additionally, courts have held that the news media status "focuses on the nature of the requester, not its request. The provision requires that the request be “made by” a representative of the news media. Id. § 552(a)(4)(A)(ii)(II). A newspaper reporter, for example, is a representative of the news media regardless of how much interest there is in the story for which he or she is requesting information." As such, the details of the request itself are moot for the purposes of determining the appropriate fee category. As such, my primary purpose is to inform about government activities by reporting on it and making the raw data available and I therefore request that fees be waived.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.


Sincerely,

M Best
An acknowledgement letter, stating the request is being processed.

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: FOIA - NARA - Murray Bookchin
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

All documents mentioning Murray Bookchin (January 14, 1921 – July 30, 2006) - political philosopher, author, and ecologist (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murray_Bookchin).

Please find evidence of his death attached and reported by The Guardian: https://www.theguardian.com/news/2006/aug/08/guardianobituaries.usa

I am confident responsive records exist for this request, due to the FBI explicitly mentioning so in a response to a previous FOIA request pertaining to records mentioning the same subject (https://cdn.muckrock.com/foia_files/2020/03/12/E10e321976e7c230e26d58c00e902bd05bf6cb121_Q77394_R355480_D2446142.pdf). See the following, including relevant reference numbers to this request: 

"Records potentially responsive to your request were transferred to the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA), and they were not previously processed pursuant to the FOIA.  You may file a request with NARA using the address above.  Please reference file numbers 100-HQ-454082 Serials 4, 6, 24, and 5; 100-HQ-454549 Serial 4-P17, 32, 42, 6-P16; 100-HQ-455596, 100-HQ-456482 Serial 9; 100-HQ-461197 Serial 13 and 2; 100-NY-166899, 62-HQ-117964 Serial 164, 88-HQ-49004 Serial 118, 76 89, 90, 91, 97, 77, 113, 145, 130, 186, and 166; 100-BS-46975 Serial 10; 100-BS-47199 Serial 1; and 100-AL-21998 Serial 435 in your correspondence."

(90) calendar days, we will administratively close* only *the portion of
your case relating to 100-HQ-454082.



All of the remaining materials require screening for categories of
information exempted from disclosure under the terms of the FOIA, prior to
public release. In particular, there are documents that may be redacted to
protect the identities of confidential sources, including FBI informant
codes and informant file numbers.



Collectively, the responsive materials in your request amount to
approximately 235 pages. Requests for FBI case files that do not exceed 700
pages are assigned to our first-tier processing queue. Taking into
consideration our existing backlog, the estimated time required to complete
the processing of your request is approximately 30 months from the date of

paper reproduction copy of the file at the cost of 80 cents per page. To
place a reproduction order, please forward this response to our office
email at specialaccess_foia@nara.gov or call 301-837-3190. A
mailing/billing address is required to generate a price quote, so please
include that information with your reproduction request.

reproduction fees. If you are unable to visit and you wish to hire a
researcher to duplicate the file, information on how to hire a researcher
can be found at this link: https://www.archives.gov/research/hire-help. The
National Archives does not endorse anyone who appears on the list.

to file an administrative appeal within ninety (90) calendar days from the
date of this letter. Appeals must be in writing and may be delivered by
regular U.S. mail or by email. By filing an appeal, you preserve your
rights under the Freedom of Information Act and present the deciding agency
with an opportunity to review your request and reconsider its decision. If
you submit your appeal by regular mail, it should be addressed to the

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Justin Tanner Petersen (Second Attempt - FBI)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Records mentioning or describing Justin Tanner Petersen AKA Agent Steal AKA Hydrerbad joker (28 July 1960 Washington, D.C. – 13 March 2010 Los Angeles, California), a hacker and informant for the Bureau. In an FBI affidavit, Petersen admitted to physically and electronically conducting illegal telephone taps and breaking into Pacific Bell's COSMOS and other companies' computer systems to check telephone numbers and determine the location of telephone lines and circuits.

Roughly 2700 pages of documentation has previously been released on Mr. Petersen, please exclude these documents from the search and provide a search of only unreleased documents. Mr. Petersen is DECEASED as of 2010 as the attached obituary from the LA times shows. Please release all reasonably segregable material which has not been previously released on this deceased subject.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Emily Crose

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Records on Militia Interactions (2017–2021, 2025–Present) Including Memos, Communications, and Substation Reports
communications.communication:
Subject: FOIA Request for U.S. Border Patrol Records on Militia Interactions (2017–2021, 2025–Present) Including Memos, Communications, and Substation Reports

Jordan Lassiter
Investigative Journalist
March 20, 2025

FOIA Officer
U.S. Customs and Border Protection
1300 Pennsylvania Avenue NW
Washington, DC 20229
Email: CBPFOIA@dhs.gov
Fax: (202) 325-1400

URGENT – LEGALLY BINDING NOTICE AND STRICT COMPLIANCE REQUIRED

This document constitutes a formal, binding request for records under the Freedom of Information Act (“FOIA”), 5 U.S.C. § 552, and the applicable regulations (28 C.F.R. Part 16). Failure to comply fully with the requirements set forth herein—including a complete search, proper preservation, and production of all responsive records—will be subject to judicial review, may be used as evidence of bad faith, and may result in immediate legal action.

I. RECORDS SUBJECT TO REQUEST

I hereby request full access to and copies of all records—without omission—that pertain to any communications, directives, or cooperative activities between U.S. Border Patrol personnel (or its representatives) and militia groups or their known leaders/members, including, but not limited to:

Arizona Border Recon (Tim Foley)
Minuteman Civil Defense Corps
United Constitutional Patriots
Veterans on Patrol

This request includes all records (such as emails, text messages, instant messages, internal memos, working notes, drafts, briefing documents, meeting minutes, contact logs, call logs, and any other communications, along with associated metadata and attachments) regarding any interaction or coordination with the above entities during the following periods:

Trump Administration – First Term: January 20, 2017 to January 20, 2021
Trump Administration – Second Term: January 20, 2025 to the present

II. DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF REQUESTED RECORDS

A. Communications and Directives

Internal Communications: All electronic or paper communications—including emails, text messages, instant messages, and internal memos (including working notes, drafts, and annotations)—exchanged among U.S. Border Patrol officials regarding any contact, coordination, or cooperation with the specified militia groups or their representatives.
External Communications: All communications (including attachments and metadata) exchanged between U.S. Border Patrol personnel and any representatives, intermediaries, or external advisors of the identified militia groups.
Interagency Communications: All communications (including memos, drafts, and internal notes) exchanged between U.S. Border Patrol personnel and other federal agencies (e.g., DHS, FBI, ICE) concerning coordination or inquiries into activities involving the specified militia groups.

B. Policy, Decision-Making, and Operational Documents

Policy Documents/Directives: All finalized and draft policies, guidelines, training materials, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and directives related to the coordination or cooperation with militia groups.
Decision-Making Records: All documents evidencing the decision-making process—including memos, meeting agendas, minutes, transcripts, internal reports, working notes, calendars, and briefing materials—that reference any interactions with the above groups.
Operational Records: Any action plans, progress reports, resource allocation documents, technical specifications, and records of any coordinated operations or intelligence-sharing activities—including all associated internal memos and supporting working documents—between Border Patrol and militia representatives.

III. CUSTODIANS, SEARCH SYSTEMS, AND TERMS

A. Custodians:

Include all records maintained or in the possession of U.S. Border Patrol officials, such as Commanding Officers, Supervisory Personnel, FOIA Officers, Records Management Officers, Field Office Administrators, and any personnel directly involved in the creation, storage, or dissemination of the requested records.

B. Search Systems:

The search must cover all electronic and paper systems, including but not limited to:

Electronic mail systems (e.g., Microsoft 365, Enterprise Vault)
Document management systems (e.g., OpenText, iManage/WorkSite)
FOIA processing systems (e.g., FOIAonline, FOIA Xpress)
Any legacy systems or locally maintained databases or repositories containing relevant records

C. Search Terms:

At a minimum, employ search queries including:

“Arizona Border Recon” OR “Tim Foley”
“Minuteman Civil Defense Corps”
“United Constitutional Patriots”
“Veterans on Patrol”
“militia” AND (“contact” OR “communication” OR “cooperation”)
“U.S. Border Patrol” AND (“militia” OR “paramilitary”)
Date range terms reflecting “2017”, “2018”, “2019”, “2020”, “2025”, and other pertinent dates
The exact syntax, Boolean operators, and any modifications applied in each search must be documented and provided.

IV. LEGAL BASIS AND PRECEDENT
This request is made pursuant to 5 U.S.C. § 552 and is supported by the following legal authorities and judicial precedents, which mandate exhaustive and complete searches for all relevant documents:

Department of Justice v. Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, 489 U.S. 749 (1989)
Milner v. Department of Navy, 562 U.S. 562 (2011)
OpenTheGovernment v. Department of Justice, 18-cv-1038 (D.D.C. May 17, 2018)
Public Citizen v. Department of Justice, 491 U.S. 440 (1989)
Truitt v. Department of State, 897 F.2d 540, 542 (D.C. Cir. 1990)
In addition, binding regulations under 28 C.F.R. Part 16 require that searches be “reasonably calculated to uncover all relevant documents.”

V. EXPEDITED PROCESSING REQUEST

I request expedited processing under 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(E)(v)(II) and 28 C.F.R. § 16.5(e) on the following grounds:

Urgency in Informing the Public: The requested records are central to investigations into potential infringements on constitutional rights and may reveal significant government overreach.
Historical and Ongoing Significance: The records span multiple administrations and are essential for determining whether current policies continue or depart from prior practices.
Media and Legal Implications: Timely disclosure is critical to ensure informed public debate and to enable judicial review if the records are improperly withheld.

VI. FEE WAIVER REQUEST

I request a full waiver of all fees associated with the processing of this request pursuant to 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(4)(A)(iii) and 28 C.F.R. § 16.10(k) because:

The disclosure of these records is in the public interest and will contribute significantly to public understanding of governmental operations and potential constitutional violations.
This request is not made for any commercial purpose.
Precedents, including Cause of Action v. Federal Trade Commission, 799 F.3d 1108 (D.C. Cir. 2015) and Carney v. U.S. Dep't of Justice, 19 F.3d 807, 814 (2d Cir. 1994), support fee waivers for requests that enhance governmental transparency.
If fees are expected to exceed $100, please contact me prior to proceeding further.

VII. FORMAT OF PRODUCTION

Records should be produced in their native electronic format, with complete metadata intact:

Emails: In formats such as .MSG or .EML with full headers, metadata, attachments, and any embedded content.
Documents: In original file formats (e.g., .DOCX, .XLSX, .PDF) with intact metadata.
Structured Data: In .CSV or .XML format, including accompanying data dictionaries.
Paper Records: High-resolution (minimum 300 dpi) color scans in PDF format.

VIII. PRESERVATION OF RECORDS

I require that all potentially responsive records be immediately preserved. This includes ensuring that all electronic files retain their original metadata and that no automated deletion or archival processes alter or destroy the relevant records.

IX. VAUGHN INDEX REQUIREMENTS

If any portion of the responsive records is withheld or redacted, I request a complete Vaughn index that:

Lists each document withheld or redacted with specificity.
Identifies the exact statutory exemption(s) claimed.
Provides a detailed explanation of how each exemption justifies the withholding, including an analysis of the potential harm from disclosure.
Discloses any segregable portions that can be released.

X. ADMINISTRATIVE TRACKING AND SEARCH DOCUMENTATION

In compliance with 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(A)(i) and relevant case law, please include with your response:

The tracking number assigned to this request.
The name(s) of the FOIA personnel responsible for processing this request.
A detailed description of the search methodology employed, including all systems, databases, repositories, and local storage locations searched.
The exact search terms used (including Boolean operators and any modifications).
Date ranges for each search.
Documentation of personnel involved and the time spent on each search.
Copies or summaries of search logs, including timestamps and result counts.
Certification by the designated Information Management Officer that all potentially responsive records were searched.

XI. RIGHT TO APPEAL AND JUDICIAL REVIEW

I expressly reserve my right to appeal any adverse determination regarding this request, including:

Denials of expedited processing or fee waivers.
Insufficient or inadequate searches.
Withholdings or redactions based on FOIA exemptions.
Any such determination shall be subject to immediate judicial review as provided under 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(4)(E) and other applicable law.

XII. PREVIOUS EVIDENCE OF INTERACTION

There is extensive, independently documented evidence of interactions between U.S. Border Patrol personnel and militia groups. Specifically:

Southern Poverty Law Center Report: In Plain Sight: Uncovering Border Patrol’s Relationship with Far-Right Militias at the Southern Border (​
SPLCENTER.ORG
) details multiple instances of such interactions in Arizona.
WIRED Report: Border Militias Prepare to Assist With Donald Trump’s Mass Deportation Plans (​
WIRED.COM
) describes contacts between militia groups like Arizona Border Recon and federal officials.
Additional Investigative Reports: Articles from the Los Angeles Times and TIME (​
LATIMES.COM
; 
TIME.COM
) corroborate historical and ongoing patterns of informal cooperation or tacit approval between Border Patrol personnel, local law enforcement, and vigilante groups.
These independent sources establish a clear pattern of interaction that underscores the public interest in obtaining full disclosure of the requested records.

XIII. SUPPLEMENTARY DOCUMENTATION AND SUBSTATION RECORDS

In addition to the records explicitly described above, please produce any supplementary or “substation” records that are relevant to the processing of this request. This includes, but is not limited to:

Additional memos, internal correspondence, briefing materials, or working documents not otherwise specifically identified herein that discuss or reference the search process, procedures, or any additional documentation related to interactions between U.S. Border Patrol and the specified militia groups.
All administrative reports, summaries, or analyses prepared by FOIA or records management personnel that elucidate the methodology, limitations, or findings related to the search for responsive records.
Any documentation from U.S. Customs and Border Protection substations located in Texas, Arizona, or any other relevant border states—including records, communications, internal memos, and operational reports—that pertain to interactions or cooperation with the aforementioned militia groups or their representatives.
Any records maintained at regional or substation offices that support the production of records responsive to this request.
Please confirm receipt of this request and provide a tracking number within five (5) working days, as required under FOIA. If any portion of this request is unclear or if additional information is required, please contact me immediately. I further request that no delay tactics or improper denials be employed.

Thank you for your prompt, full, and legally compliant disclosure of these records.

Respectfully,

Jordan Lassiter
Investigative Journalist

communications.subject: RE: Freedom of Information Act Request #CBP-FO-2025-088795
communications.communication:
Subject: FOIA Appeal – Unlawful Closure and Inadequate Search for Request on U.S. Border Patrol and Militia Interactions

To: FOIA Appeals Officer
U.S. Customs and Border Protection
1300 Pennsylvania Avenue NW
Washington, DC 20229
Email: CBPFOIA@dhs.gov
Fax: (202) 325-1400

From:
Jordan Lassiter
Investigative Journalist
March 23, 2025

RE: Appeal of Arbitrary Closure and Failure to Conduct Proper Search (FOIA Request: Records on U.S. Border Patrol and Militia Interactions 2017–2021, 2025–Present)

I. INTRODUCTION

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act (“FOIA”), 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(A)(i), I formally appeal the arbitrary closure and inadequate processing of my FOIA request seeking records concerning communications, memos, and reports related to U.S. Border Patrol’s interactions with militia groups from 2017–2021 and 2025–present.

CBP has failed to conduct a reasonable search for responsive records, failed to issue a proper determination, and arbitrarily closed my request without adequate justification. This constitutes a clear violation of FOIA’s statutory mandates, as established in Truitt v. Department of State, 897 F.2d 540, 542 (D.C. Cir. 1990), which requires agencies to conduct searches “reasonably calculated to uncover all relevant documents.”

II. BASIS FOR APPEAL

A. Failure to Conduct an Adequate Search

CBP has not demonstrated that it undertook a search that meets FOIA’s standards, nor has it provided the search methodologies, custodians, systems searched, or search terms used. The agency is legally required to document these details (OpenTheGovernment v. Department of Justice, 18-cv-1038 (D.D.C. May 17, 2018)), and its failure to do so suggests an inadequate or nonexistent search.

B. Unlawful Closure Without a Proper Determination

FOIA requires agencies to provide a written determination that includes the scope of the search and an explanation for any records withheld or redacted. The arbitrary closure of my request without a Vaughn Index, a justification for any exemptions, or a record of the search methodology violates Milner v. Department of Navy, 562 U.S. 562 (2011), and Public Citizen v. Department of Justice, 491 U.S. 440 (1989).

C. Failure to Address Request Scope and Mandatory Custodian Searches

I specifically outlined required search parameters, including:
	•	Custodians: Commanding Officers, FOIA Officers, Field Office Administrators, and others involved in record creation or storage.
	•	Systems: Email servers (Microsoft 365, Enterprise Vault), document repositories (OpenText, iManage), FOIA processing systems (FOIAonline, FOIA Xpress), and relevant databases.
	•	Search Terms: “Arizona Border Recon,” “Minuteman Civil Defense Corps,” “United Constitutional Patriots,” “Veterans on Patrol,” and other related terms.

CBP has not addressed whether these required elements were searched, violating FOIA’s mandate for a complete and reasonable effort.

III. REQUESTED REMEDIES
	1.	Immediate Reopening of My FOIA Request
CBP must properly reopen and process my request instead of arbitrarily closing it without fulfilling its obligations under FOIA.
	2.	A Complete and Adequate Search
CBP must conduct a full search, including all electronic systems, paper records, emails, and other documentation, and provide a detailed explanation of search methodologies.
	3.	A Legally Compliant Determination with Vaughn Index (if applicable)
If any records are withheld, CBP must provide a Vaughn Index detailing each document withheld, the exemptions applied, and a justification for each exemption.
	4.	Immediate Production of Responsive Records
Given the strong public interest in government interactions with militia groups, I request that all non-exempt records be released as soon as possible.
	5.	Compliance with FOIA’s Statutory Timeframe
CBP must issue a proper response within 20 working days per 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(A)(ii).

IV. CONCLUSION

CBP’s arbitrary closure and failure to conduct an adequate search violate FOIA’s legal requirements. I request immediate corrective action, including reopening the request, performing a proper search, and providing responsive records. Failure to comply may result in legal action to compel compliance.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and provide a response within the statutory timeframe.

Sincerely,
Jordan Lassiter
Investigative Journalist

communications.subject: FOIA appeal CBP-AP-2025-002676 (Status Update)
communications.communication:
Dear Mr. Lassiter, 

I am reaching out to provide you an update on your FOIA appeal CBP-AP-2025-002676 (appeal of FOIA request CBP-FO-2025-088795). 

Under 6 CFR 5.5(c), “whenever the statutory time limits for processing a request cannot be met because of 'unusual circumstances,' as defined in the FOIA, and the component extends the time limits on that basis, the component shall, before expiration of the twenty-day period to respond, notify the requester in writing of the unusual circumstances involved and of the date by which processing of the request can be expected to be completed.” I am reaching out to provide you with this notification. 

Due to the necessity for consultation with multiple offices within CBP, we are extending the deadline to respond to your appeal. The estimated time frame for completion of your appeal is by mid-June; however, this is subject to change depending on any delay in response regarding the consultations. You will receive an additional status notification if the time frame must be extended past mid-June. 

Your appeal is a priority, and we will make every effort to respond to your appeal as soon as possible. Thank you for your patience. 

Sincerely, 
CBP FOIA Appeals

communications.subject: DC Freedom of Information Act Request: "The Panorama Pipe Cover-Up: Ward 8 Landslide Engineering & MS4 Permit Violations" (District Department of Transportation)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the DC Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

To: ddot.foia@dc.gov, doee.foia@dc.gov, hq.foia@epa.gov, r3public@epa.gov 

CC: neelima.ghanta@dc.gov, alisoun.hughes@dc.gov, david.dickman@dc.gov, lindsey.appiah@dc.gov, tomas.talamante@dc.gov, pmendelson@dccouncil.us​, callen@dccouncil.gov, rwhite@dccouncil.gov,​  swilson@dccouncil.gov, eugene.​adams@dc.gov ldonovan@wusa9.com, chernande1@wusa9.com​,tkopania@wusa9.com

Subject: EXPEDITED FOIA DEMAND: Historic Stormwater Pipe Installation, NPDES Violations & MS4 Financial Records (1600 Morris Rd SE Corridor)

To the District Department of Transportation (DDOT), Department of Energy & Environment (DOEE), and the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) National FOIA Office:

Under the District of Columbia Freedom of Information Act (D.C. Official Code § 2-531 et seq.) and the federal Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. § 552), I am formally requesting copies of specific infrastructure, environmental compliance, and financial records. 

CLARIFICATION OF DISTINCT REQUEST:
Please be advised that this request is entirely separate and distinct from my prior FOIA submissions regarding the 25-foot structural landslide, hillside runoff, and biological mitigation (tree plantings) at this location. This specific request targets the physical, engineered installation of a surface-laid stormwater drainage pipe and the corresponding federal financial audits tied to its approval. 

THE INFRASTRUCTURE IN QUESTION:
I am requesting all historic engineering plans, work orders, site surveys, and structural blueprints regarding the installation of a corrugated plastic stormwater pipe, anchored by a poured concrete collar, originating from the ridge vantage point of 1600 Morris Rd SE (in the immediate vicinity of the ​"Famous Panorama Room​"). This botched, surface-laid municipal infrastructure descends directly down the steep, wooded terrain and terminates at the active 25-foot landslide directly adjacent to the residential foundation of 1490 Morris Rd SE. 

FEDERAL COMPLIANCE & FINANCIAL RECORDS SOUGHT:
This request seeks to uncover how this substandard engineering passed rigorous environmental standards, and why only basic amounts of financing and oversight were approved for this catastrophic municipal failure in Ward 8. Therefore, I am requesting​ from January 1, 1980, to the date this request is processed:
1. All environmental impact assessments and compliance documents demonstrating how this specific plastic-and-concrete pipe installation met the rigorous standards of the Federal Clean Water Act (33 U.S.C. § 1251 et seq.), the National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES), and the District's Phase I Municipal Separate Storm Sewer System (MS4) permit.

2. All financial records, DOEE Stormwater Enterprise Fund ledgers, and EPA grant allocations detailing the exact amount of capital funding approved for this specific hillside stormwater management project versus the funds actually deployed to the corridor. 

3. All records, illicit discharge reports, and municipal assessments detailing how this severed pipeline acts as the direct hydro-engine drowning the residential properties at 1490 Morris Rd SE, 1488 Morris Rd SE, and the 2210-2260 Hunter Pl SE corridor.

4. All health, safety, and water testing records connecting this botched hillside stormwater management to the creation and maintenance of the illegal, disease-laden, and unprotected surface water pond located downstream at 2322 16th St SE and 2351 16th St SE (as designated on municipal Google Maps data), which sits actively within a designated Safe Schools zone. 

NOTICE OF FEDERAL ESCALATION:
This FOIA serves as the foundational data pull for a forthcoming financial audit. If the engineering records confirm this infrastructure fails to meet federal CWA and MS4 standards—and is directly responsible for the flooding and structural decay of the aforementioned addresses—we will be opening formal inquiries with the EPA Office of Inspector General (OIG) and the Department of Justice (DOJ) Environment and Natural Resources Division to follow the municipal money and uncover exact points of administrative malfeasance. 

FORMAT & FEE WAIVER DEMAND:
I require all digital records, financial ledgers, and architectural blueprints to be provided in their native, rich-metadata electronic formats. Do not strip EXIF data or GIS coordinates, and do not sanitize responsive records into flat PDFs. I am requesting a total waiver of all search, review, and duplication fees, as these records are sought strictly to inform the public of systemic municipal negligence, financial mismanagement, and severe public safety threats within a Safe Schools zone. 

Furthermore, this formal request is being uploaded to MuckRock.com for immediate public transparency. WUSA9 investigative journalists and photojournalists are copied on this communication to document how the District and federal oversight agencies respond to the discovery of structurally failed, unpermitted hillside infrastructure.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 15 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

FRED GAMBLE JR

District of Columbia

title: Civil Standby/Custody Exchange Assist Call on 09/23/2026 at 1016 Kurth Drive

communications.subject: Texas Public Information Act Request: Civil Standby/Custody Exchange Assist Call on 09/23/2026 at 1016 Kurth Drive
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Texas Public Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

All Incident and/or offense reports or other written records comprising the main narrative report that the responding officers filed, including officer name/badge number, case or incident number, disposition, and any supplemental narratives added later--regarding an apparent civil standby/custody exchange assist call to 1016 Kurth Drive in Lufkin, Texas on September 23, 2026 at approximately 6:15 pm involving Michael and Ashton Rhoden.

All Computer-Aided Dispatch (CAD) log and/or "calls for service" records—or other timestamped dispatch record showing when the call came in, unit(s) assigned, arrival/departure times, and call disposition codes--regarding an apparent civil standby/custody exchange assist call to 1016 Kurth Drive in Lufkin, Texas on September 23, 2026 at approximately 6:15 pm involving Michael and Ashton Rhoden.

All field notes and/or supplemental reports— or any other handwritten or typed notes officers took on scene including follow-up reports of other officers and supervisors involved--regarding an apparent civil standby/custody exchange assist call to 1016 Kurth Drive in Lufkin, Texas on September 23, 2026 at approximately 6:15 pm involving Michael and Ashton Rhoden.

Any witness and/or party statements—or other written statements taken from family members and/or bystanders present during said exchange.

Any photos officers took of the scene, vehicles, or parties during said exchange.

Any use-of-force and/or incident-review reports--or other records of any physical intervention occurred including any internal complaint or IA (internal affairs) records tied to the responding officers' conduct, to the extent legally releasable--pertaining to said exchange.

All body-worn camera (BWC) footage from every officer who responded to an apparent civil standby/custody exchange assist call to 1016 Kurth Drive in Lufkin, Texas on September 23, 2026 at approximately 6:15 pm involving Michael and Ashton Rhoden.

Any dash/in-car camera video from patrol vehicles on scene during said exchange.

Any 911 call audio or other original recorded call(s) that generated the dispatch for said exchange assistance.

Any radio and/or dispatch traffic recordings—and any other audio recordings of the back-and-forth between dispatch and units, separate from the 911 call itself--pertaining to an apparent civil standby/custody exchange assist call to 1016 Kurth Drive in Lufkin, Texas on September 23, 2026 at approximately 6:15 pm involving Michael and Ashton Rhoden.

Any surveillance and/or third-party video the department collected in the course of facilitating said exchange--including but not limited to doorbell and/or business camera footage pulled into the case file regarding an apparent civil standby/custody exchange assist call to 1016 Kurth Drive in Lufkin, Texas on September 23, 2026 at approximately 6:15 pm involving Michael and Ashton Rhoden.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Joel  Lambright

title: Sydney Lucas Arrest – Body-Worn Camera and Video Records

communications.subject: Florida Sunshine Law Request: Sydney Lucas Arrest – Body-Worn Camera and Video Records
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Florida Sunshine Law, I hereby request the following records:

Incident date: August 21, 2026
Individual involved: Sydney Lucas
Location: Irish Kevin’s, 211 Duval Street, Key West, Florida

All publicly releasable audiovisual and photographic records relating to the Key West Police Department incident and arrest involving Sydney Lucas on August 21, 2026, at or near Irish Kevin’s on Duval Street.

Specifically:

• Complete, unedited body-worn camera (BWC) footage from every KWPD officer who responded to, participated in, assisted with, transported, or documented the incident/arrest.
• All dash-camera/in-car video and associated audio from police vehicles involved.
• All surveillance/security-camera footage obtained by KWPD, including footage received from Irish Kevin’s or surrounding businesses.
• All photographs, videos, and audiovisual evidence collected or created by KWPD in connection with the incident, including photographs/scans/video of the allegedly fraudulent identification and other physical evidence.
• Any available audio/video of transportation or transfer of custody following the arrest maintained by KWPD.
• The corresponding incident/offense report, arrest/probable-cause affidavit, supplemental reports, and CAD/dispatch report, including records identifying all responding officers.

Please provide video in its original electronic format and highest reasonably available quality, rather than screenshots or transcripts. If portions are exempt, please provide all reasonably segregable non-exempt portions and identify the statutory basis for any redactions or withholding.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Nick Wong

communications.subject: RE:  [EXTERNAL] Florida Sunshine Law Request: Sydney Lucas Arrest – Body-Worn Camera and Video Records
communications.communication:
Thank you for your public records request.

Please be advised that KWPD Records Section no longer handles requests for body-worn camera or dash camera footage, photos, 911 audio calls, police radio communications and use of force records. All these types of requests are forwarded to and fulfilled by the Public Affairs Liaison.

Your request will therefore be forwarded to the Public Affairs Liaison for review and processing. She will handle the request and provide any responsive records in accordance with applicable public records requirements.

Thank you for your understanding.

Respectfully,



Chawana McDowell
Lead Records Clerk | Key West Police Department |
Records Section |

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Coachella Valley Unified School District Reports-Cal. Gov’t Code § 8310.5
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Please provide, from the year 2017 to the present, all reports that CVUSD has submitted to the State of California or federal government, pursuant to the legal requirements found in 709(c) of Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, as amended, 42 U.S.C. 2000e-8(c), 29 CFR 1602.39 and .41-.45, and Cal. Gov’t Code § 8310.5. In summary, the above laws require school districts to report the racial/ethnic make up of teachers in the district, and are commonly known as EEO-5 reports.

This request seeks, from the year 2017 to the present, all reports (including but not limited to EEO-5 reports), spreadsheets, or other similar documents which CVUSD has given to the State of California or federal government, which reflects the racial and/or ethnic make up of teaching staff.

Sincerely,

Annette Harings

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

communications.subject: Indiana Access to Public Records Act Request: Derek McHatton (Edgewood Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Indiana Access to Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Records related to the following current or former employees:

Derek McHatton (9909-5890)

Hiring date, termination date, compensation, commendations, assignments/job roles, disciplinary actions, factual basis for disciplinary actions and letters of resignation for the following employees. Please exclude copies of individual training certificates.

I am including the following information as a helpful reference to related case law and Public Access Counselor opinions regarding personnel records of public employees:

https://public.courts.in.gov/Decisions/api/Document/Opinion?Id=QPNIyLTvnhzxDZhO52J1KCEs4fPOKpLR0hAitsADZUhV--IpFNWE224Cxiw0N3jJ0

Indiana Supreme Court decision WTHR-TV v. Hamilton Southeastern School District states that APRA requires disclosure of the factual basis for disciplinary action, and that factual basis cannot be a bald conclusion. It also has to be sufficient for a reasonable person to understand what an employee did to deserve discipline. See the opinion starting on page 7 of the link above.

A passing reference to violation of a specific policy is not sufficient to meet this standard.

The Indiana Public Access Counselor also has addressed the topic of resignations in lieu of termination. One such opinion can be reviewed here, but simply put a resignation in lieu of a termination does not dissolve an agency’s responsibility to provide the factual basis for discipline under the public records statute.

The state’s records statute applies to all employees, regardless of wither they are probationary or not.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 7 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Emily Hopkins

communications.subject: The Kansas Open Records Act Request: Pittsburg Flock Safety Records - Thru August 2026
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the The Kansas Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

1) Any emails, written communications, documents, contracts, invoices, presentations, or other communications between officials or employees from the City of Pittsburg (The City) and officials or employees from the company "Flock Safety."

2) I request internal training documents and policies and procedures for the use of "Flock Safety" tools.

3) I request any sharing agreements signed with other agencies as well as The City's sharing agreement it requires other agencies to conform to.

5) I request the web address of The City's "Flock Safety" transparency portal, a free feature of Flock OS.

6) Lastly, I request all available audit data from the "Flock Safety" audit tools. This should include the organization audit, network audit, and sharing report.
    A. Organization Audit in Flock.
    The report should include data logged from the period of installation to the date this request is processed. Per Flock's documentation, the Organization Audit is available within the Insights tab and is defined as searches done by the City.

    B. Network Audit in Flock.
    The report should include data logged from the period of installation, to the date this request is processed. Per Flock's documentation, the Network Audit is available within the Insights tab and is defined as searches of the City’s Flock network by any agency the City has shared with in the Flock System.

    C. Sharing report in Flock.
    The report should include flock networks shared with The City and networks The City is sharing its network with.

Flock Safety maintains documentation on these reports. Flock documentation says the reports can be pulled in 31 day increments.  Flock also says that customers may want to contact support for requests longer than six months or for large accounts. If production of audit logs requires support from Flock, please declare such needs and have the City's point person on the Flock support ticket provide updates on their progress.  

I request that files be supplied in their original electronic, machine readable format rather than being converted to any alternate formats.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

communications.subject: RE: The Kansas Open Records Act Request: Pittsburg KS Flock Safety Records
communications.communication:
Hi Tammy,

I'd like to confirm a few things regarding the cost and your (the city's) obligations as outlined in K.S.A. 45-219.

I would like confirmation that the rates provided, $25.20 per hour for IT staff and $30 per hour for PPD staff, meet the requirements in full as outlined in K.S.A. 45-219(c). In particular, K.S.A. 45-219(c)(3), which states that "the agency shall use in good faith the lowest-cost category of staff reasonably necessary to provide access to or furnish copies of public records. Charges for staff time shall be based on the employee's salary or hourly wage. Charges for staff time shall not include the costs of employee benefits." Additionally, per K.S.A. 45-219(c)(4), I would like an itemized statement for the following parts of my request: 1, 2, 3, 6A, 6B, and 6C. These itemized statements should include the hourly rate and time to furnish the records and separately the hourly rate and time to review and redact the records as well as include any other costs for these records.

Pursuant to K.S.A. 45-219(e)(1), since these requests exceed five hours and the estimated actual cost exceeds $200, I would like to remind you of your obligations to "make reasonable efforts to contact the requester and engage in interactive communication about mitigating costs to fill the request." I would be open to discussions to help mitigate costs for the request while maintaining as much of the original request as possible. For example, if there have been portions of my request that have been fulfilled by previous requests, a copy of those requests would suffice, and what is covered by the provided copies may be omitted from my request.

Thanks,
Shelby
