title: Sheriff use of force data (2017-2025) (Thurston County Sheriff)

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: Sheriff use of force data (2017-2025) (Thurston County Sheriff)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Use of force (UOF) data dating from January 1, 2017 to December 31, 2025. If possible, please provide this data in database or spreadsheet format and include the case number, incident date, incident time, subject injured indicator, subject injury force related info (e.g. Yes or No), subject age, subject gender, subject ethnicity, subject weapon type, incident area occurred, force type, officer division (e.g. law enforcement operations, detention/correctional operations, etc.), badge number and names associated with the officers involved. If one or more of these fields or dates is unavailable, provide all fields and/or information that is available responsive to my request. If no database or spreadsheet format is available, please provide copies of each individual use of force report or other report where use of force information is documented/reported by officers. Note, this is for all use of force incidents reported by your agency, not limited to only those incidents required to be reported under state or federal programs.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Samuel Sinyangwe

title: Flock Network and Audit Logs Dunwoody GA

communications.subject: Georgia Open Records Act Request: Flock Network and Audit Logs Dunwoody GA
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Georgia Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

I am requesting copies of all audit logs, search logs, or usage reports related to your agency's use of Flock "ALPR" systems for the period of April 1st through when this request is received. This includes but is not limited to: Records of license plate searches performed by agency personnel Timestamps of searches User identification information (names, badge numbers, or user IDs) Any associated case numbers or investigation references Some of these records may be available as the "Organization Audit" and "Network Audit" in the Flock software's "Insights" section. 

Please provide records in their original electronic format (CSV, Excel, or similar) where possible. The audit logs can be accessed via your agency's Flock admin dashboard on the "Insights" tab. These logs may show the date/time of search, user ID, and search parameters and reason. Customers may download these logs in the user interface as spreadsheets in 31-day increments. It is recommended that Flock customer support assist customers with the downloads when feasible for timeframes larger than six months and major accounts.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jason Hunyar

Dear Jason Hunyar, 
I am in receipt of your open records request. Please log in to your portal to access all documents on file with the City of Dunwoody that are responsive to your request.  As this request contains license plate data not subject to public disclosure per O.C.G.A. § 35-1-22(f), all sensitive information therein has been redacted. Pursuant to OCGA Sec. 50-18-71(b)(1)(A), some, but not all, of the data requested is immediately available. Specifically, the data contained in Colum G is not immediately available, as a line-by-line determination of whether the information contained in this column for each row will require further review to determine whether that information is subject to an exemption under the Open Records Act. Accordingly, we have redacted that column of the data for now on suspicion that many of the cells within Colum G are likely subject to redaction under OCGA 50-18-72(a)(3) or (a)(4). 
Could you please clarify what you mean by an “organization audit,” and what specific prior production you are referring to in your 6/19/2026 response? 
Best, 
Eric Shealy Records Clerk Dunwoody Open Records Center City of Dunwoody 4800 Ashford Dunwoody Road Dunwoody, Georgia 30338 (P) 678-382-6716

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: TechStat presentations and reports
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

1) All final Investment Review Board presentations for TechStat reviews conducted by DOI from Jan. 1, 2022 until the date this request is processed. More information about IRB presentations can be found in the attached guide.

2) All memos of record, or comparable final reports and action items from IRB meetings, for TechStat reviews conducted by DOI from Jan. 1, 2022 until the date this request is processed. More information about TechStat memos of record can be found in the attached guide.

I ask that all fees be waived as I am a journalist and intend to used the requested records to publish articles in the public interest and not for any commercial purpose.

If you choose to impose fees, I request a detailed breakdown of the fees, including the hourly wage of each employee involved and an explanation of the employee hours required to fulfill the request.

If you choose to reject this request or redact portions of responsive documents, I ask that you provide a detailed breakdown of the statutory exemptions and associated case law underlying your decision to withhold each/any portions from public review.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Todd Feathers

communications.subject: The Missouri Sunshine Law Request: Emails to/from Flock Safety from OCT2025 breach
communications.communication:
Good morning,

The Brookfield Police Department has completed a search of department email
records for the requested time frame of September 21, 2025, through
December 1, 2025, including searches for emails containing the terms
“Flock” and “Flock Safety,” as well as emails sent to or received from
Flock Safety.

The records located through the Brookfield Police Department's search are
attached for your review. These records constitute the responsive email
records located within the possession and control of the Brookfield Police
Department. Responsive email threads and available attachments have been
included where applicable.

With regard to the portion of your Missouri Sunshine Law request concerning
records of the North Missouri Drug Task Force, including the Drug Task
Force Officer's email records, please be advised that the Brookfield Police
Department does not maintain or house records of the North Missouri Drug
Task Force and does not have access to the Drug Task Force Officer's email
records.

Pursuant to § 610.023.1, RSMo., each public governmental body is required
to designate a custodian of records who is responsible for the maintenance
of that governmental body's records. Because the Brookfield Police
Department does not maintain or have access to the North Missouri Drug Task
Force's email records, those records are not within the possession or
control of the Brookfield Police Department and cannot be produced by this
department.

Accordingly, the attached records reflect the responsive records located
through the Brookfield Police Department's search.

Thank you.

*Khaylee Niemeier*
Police Clerk
Brookfield Police Department
Office: 660.258.3385

communications.subject: Nevada Public Records Act Request: LVMPD Price Retention
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Nevada Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

This is a new request and is narrower than, and distinct from, my request of 17 May 2026, reference X010952-051726, which your office closed on 19 May 2026 with the response "No records were located."

I am not seeking the case file. I am seeking the Department's own records governing the retention and disposition of records of that type and era:

1. The records retention and disposition schedule or schedules in effect for LVMPD incident, event, case and death-investigation reports generated in 1975, together with any subsequent schedule that governed the disposition of 1975-era reports.

2. Any certificate of destruction, destruction log, disposal authorization, or equivalent record documenting the destruction or other disposition of LVMPD incident, event or case reports from calendar year 1975.

3. Any record describing the transfer of 1975-era LVMPD reports to another custodian, including the Nevada State Library, Archives and Public Records, or any successor agency, and the date of any such transfer.

4. Any policy, procedure or index describing where 1975-era LVMPD records are currently held, if they are held at all.

These records are separate from the case file that was the subject of the earlier request. My earlier request asked, in the alternative, for destruction documentation and retention authority, and the 19 May response did not address that portion. Whether the report never existed or was lawfully destroyed on a schedule are different facts, and this request seeks the records that establish which is the case.

If any portion is exempt, please identify the specific statutory basis for the withholding as required by NRS 239.0107.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jerome McClure

communications.subject: RE: Nevada Public Records Act Request #X016105-082126
communications.communication:
Thank you for the DRM Retrieval Locations sheet and the June 2020 inventory email. Read against my original request, three points remain open, and I would be grateful to have them treated as a continuation of this request rather than a new one.

Item 1 asked for the retention schedule in effect for 1975-era reports. The schedule provided is dated 2021. If an earlier schedule governed the 1971 through 1979 event files, or authorized their destruction, please provide it. If the 2021 schedule is the authority under which they were purged, please say so.

Item 2 asked for disposition records. The DRM sheet lists 1971 through 1979 event files as "Purged Files." Please provide any destruction log, certificate of destruction, or disposal approval for that purge, and its date or date range. If none exists, please say so.

The June 2020 email states that "there are backups at the vault" for the event paperwork from 1971 through 1985. Do the backup reels for 1971 through 1979 still exist? If they were destroyed, when, and under what authority? Item 3 of my request, on transfer to another custodian such as the Nevada State Library, Archives and Public Records, also did not receive a response, and applies to these reels as well.

Thank you.

communications.subject: Michigan Freedom of Information Act Request: DRMM monitoring (updated)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Michigan Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

All completed programmatic monitoring reports, completed monitoring checklists or tools, corrective action plans, provider responses to corrective actions, and follow-up or verification reports prepared or maintained by the City of Detroit Human, Homeless, and Family Services Department concerning Detroit Rescue Mission Ministries from January 1, 2026 through the date of this request.

This request is a resubmission of FOIA request 2603656 (attached). In the City’s August 7, 2026 response, the City stated that the requested reports were “still in the process of being completed” and asked that the request be resubmitted at a later date.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Aaron Mondry

communications.subject: Fw: [EXTERNAL] Michigan Freedom of Information Act Request: DRMM monitoring (updated)
communications.communication:
This email serves as the City of Detroit’s response to the above-referenced matter. Your request was received at the City of Detroit Law Department Freedom of Information 26Act Section via facsimile or email during the period September 11, 2026 through September 13, 2026. Because your request was received by electronic transmission, pursuant to Section 5(1) of the Michigan Freedom of Information Act (the “Act”), MCL 15.235(1); it is deemed to have been received at the Law Department on the next business day, September 14, 2026.

Pursuant to Section 5(2) of the Act, MCL 15.235(2), the City’s response is due within five (5) business days. However, due to the nature and the scope of your request and the volume of the requests received by the City, we are extending the City’s response deadline by ten (10) additional business days in accordance with Section 5(2) (d) of the Act, MCL 15.235(2) (d). Therefore, your request will be granted, denied, or granted in part and denied in part on or before October 5, 2026.

Your request is being handled by Devin Farrelly. If you have questions regarding your request, or if you did not provide an email address in your request, please forward it to Devin Farrelly at farrellyd@detroitmi.gov<mailto:farrellyd@detroitmi.gov> to provide you a response more readily than by regular mail or fax. Mail and fax are not preferred at this time since they both require in-office support. We thank you in advance for your understanding.
